title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching, caching, quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: reduce unit inference cost by providing safe, production-ready defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching and by exposing quantization profile recommendations. Additionally add a unit-economics (uecon) tooling endpoint and CLI to help SREs and customers simulate cost impact before rollout. This PR implements an autotune defaults engine that picks batching windows, cache TTL heuristics, and quant profiles per model class + workload signal, and integrates a uecon tool that computes per-request and per-token cost after autosettings. Backfills telemetry to validate estimations.
commits: feat(autotune): add defaults engine and heuristics (aisha/engine-defaults) - initial implementation and tests
refactor(batching): extract batch_window estimator and add conservative fallback for cold starts
feat(uecon): add /internal/uecon CLI and HTTP endpoint + cost simulator
chore(config): add quant-profile catalog and mapping table for common open models
test: add integration tests simulating mixed request size workloads and cost assertions
fix(ci): pin go-test timeout for flaky runtime scheduling test
changed_files: service/autotune/defaults.go - new autotune defaults and selection logic
runtime/batching/batcher.go - refactor: expose estimator interface; small logic change to limit max batch-window to 120ms
runtime/caching/prefix_cache.go - add adaptive TTL heuristics and prefix hit accounting
api/internal/uecon/handler.go - HTTP endpoint for unit-econ simulations
docs/reference/autotune.md - docs for defaults and safety checks
telemetry/metrics/autotune_metrics.yaml - add metrics for estimated_vs_actual_cost, chosen_quant_profile
configs/quant_profiles.yaml - quantization profile catalog for 4-bit/8-bit variants
sdk/python/examples/uecon_example.ipynb - small notebook showing cost projections
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, a quantization profile catalog, and a unit-economics simulator (CLI + HTTP). Customers can preview cost impact of autotune settings before enabling. No behavioral changes by default; settings are gated behind a feature flag.
